events.text_en: Nhan Tề Phi falls at the head of Lạc Hà's field on Chiết Kích Nguyên; her disciple Cảnh Trường Thiên brings her body off the plain at night.
The last of the maples Nhan Cô Vụ planted round Lạc Hà's hall dies in a dry summer; the elder Chử Hồng Diệp boils its sap, and a note in the founder's hand is found in the canon's margin.
Lạc Hà Tông borrows from its vassal Thiên Bảo Trai to raise a new seat; Phan Vật Hoa names the interest, and the head names the surety in private.
Quách Tiếp Vân lays the Cloud Bridge Array across the gorge of Vân Kiều Trấn, where the miners' rope bridge broke, to a design bought from Vệ Văn Cơ.
Lạc Hà Tông leaves the steppe for the mountain town of Vân Kiều; its old hall becomes the outer gate, Cựu Hà Viện.
Tô Vãn Chiếu puts the move of the seat to Lạc Hà's elders at dusk; Trầm Tịch Dương and Hình Trọng Sơn vote against it, and it is carried.
Hình Lạc Nhạn walks three hundred paces into the miasma of Chiết Kích Nguyên after the lost Tân Khẩu boy and comes back with his shoe.
On the burned landing at Đào Sa, Lạc Hà's raid leader Lô Xướng Vãn helps a ferryman's son fish nails out of the river, and takes him home.
Lô Tiểu Ca meets the Tùng Đào raiders' leader on the last rope bridge of the Ngư Ca border; he dies there, and she falls when the ropes go. The Tang Ma weavers hang her lamp from the new bridge.
Lạc Hà's fleet master Hạ Hầu Trường Phong moors his ships across the harbour mouth of Thôn Hải Môn and burns with his flagship when the pirates' fire-rafts come out.
Thiệu Song Phong, who forged the iron gates of Thiết Tỏa Quan, dies holding them so the allies can get off the river road.
At the truce, Nhan Cô Vụ cuts the ninth verse from the boats' song and names the vein below his hall for his daughter: Tề Phi Mạch.
